correctness.rationale: KRep complement is c.e. on finite effective models by a finite tuple of false-theory witnesses per world; satisfaction and H-membership are decidable. In the many-one reduction, H_e is the all-assignment theory over the zero assignment and halting-stage activated singleton assignments; membership reduces to finitely many syntactic atom indices and bounded simulations. The one-world frame satisfies all six Nishimura conditions; reflexive representation if and only if e does not halt. For halting e, box-bottom distinguishes the empty successor relation, and box-negated-p_n distinguishes the looping relation. Reconstructed algebraic closure laws and frame-level quantification. The attached checker completed 44,624 finite assertions; the universal theorem follows from the proof, not the tests.

value.rationale: The exact Pi01 index-set classification is a decision frontier for the new canonical KRep semantic representation test. It identifies finite certificates for negative instances and rules out a uniform recognition decider even at one world, with all modal normality frame principles and a primitive-recursive true closure operation. This is materially distinct from deciding satisfiability of individual modal formulas or from explicit finite closure tables; the latter boundary is specified.
